questions.resolution_criteria: Source of Truth : Official national government announcements or reliable news reporting published by July 25, 2026. Resolution Condition : Identify the European country whose national government declares a national emergency because of wildfires between July 1 and July 25, 2026. Regional or local emergency declarations alone do not qualify. Accepted Answer Format : The country's commonly used English name.
questions.current_reasoning: Major 2026-07-21 European wildfire & government-response update with 4 days left in the July 1-25 window (ABC.es, El Pais, EFE, RTVE, Reuters/Straits Times, Al Jazeera, AFP/HT, NDTV): (1) Spain drops sharply (0.45 -> 0.31, still #1) after three de-escalatory institutional signals on Tuesday July 21: Castilla-La Mancha explicitly rejected PP's request to elevate La Mierla to Nivel 3 national emergency ('no va a cambiar nada'), Spain's weekly Consejo de Ministros met without declaring a national emergency (spokeswoman Elma Saiz only urged prudence), and El Pais reported La Mierla (~30,000-32,000 ha) shifting from defensive to offensive/stabilization with Deputy PM Sara Aagesen stating 'zona gravemente afectada' comes after extinction; Spain still leads because its 40-44C third heatwave (+5.3C anomaly) persists through July 23 alongside a new Level 2 fire in Selas (Guadalajara) and blazes in Teruel. (2) Portugal rises (0.20 -> 0.23, #2): exposed to the same July 21-24 Iberian heatwave, already under mainland State of Alert since July 3, with a unitary-government escalation bar to State of Calamity/Contingency far lower than Spain's autonomous-region standoff. (3) Greece surges (0.10 -> 0.17, #3): Reuters July 21 reports Greece entering its first peak-summer 40C heatwave at +5.8C above normal—the highest temperature anomaly in Europe—right across July 21-25. (4) France enters the top 5 at 0.07 (replacing Italy): two firefighters were killed on July 21 in a Gironde blaze (3 firefighter deaths in two weeks), a fast-moving 1,700-ha Var blaze forced ~400 evacuations with 900-950 firefighters deployed, and EFFIS confirmed >42,000 ha burned YTD (worst mid-July season since record 2022), though capped by France's high constitutional bar for national emergencies. (5) North Macedonia drops (0.09 -> 0.05, #5): retains July 2024/2025 state-of-crisis precedent, but Reuters July 21 reports the Western Balkans shifting from heatwave to hailstorms spreading across Bosnia and southern Serbia directly into North Macedonia. Retaining 17% residual for Italy (~3.5%), Bulgaria (~3%), Cyprus (~2.5%), Albania (~2.5%, 42C in Tirana July 21), Croatia, Montenegro, Serbia, Turkey, and Romania.

local_articles.snippet: MIAMI - The basketball world was ablaze on the morning of July 22 after the Miami Heat’s YouTube account mistakenly posted a video the night before teasing the possible return of LeBron James, who has yet to announce where he will play his 24th NBA season. local_articles.title: Inter Miami sign Casemiro as MLS opens tampering investigation
local_articles.snippet: July 22 - Inter Miami announced the signing of Brazil midfielder Casemiro as a free agent on Wednesday, but Major League Soccer said it was investigating a "tampering allegation" against the club. The league's probe cast a shadow over the midfielder's arrival, with MLS saying it would withhold details of a settlement between Inter Miami and LA Galaxy over Casemiro's discovery rights until the review concludes. Inter Miami said they had signed the five-time Champions League winner - who left Manchester United at the end of last season - on a deal through the 2027 MLS Sprint campaign, with an option to extend to June 2029. Yet the league then said in a statement that it had launched an investigation and was gathering all relevant information and would refrain from further comment until the review was complete. local_articles.title: Why is MLS reviewing Inter Miami over Casemiro transfer? Tampering allegation against club explained
local_articles.snippet: Major League Soccer (MLS) has opened a review into an allegation that Inter Miami broke league rules while signing former Manchester United midfielder Casemiro. The issue is linked to MLS’ Discovery Priority system, which gives clubs the first right to negotiate with certain players. According to ESPN’s Lizzy Becherano, the LA Galaxy filed a tampering claim after alleging that Inter Miami contacted Casemiro before securing his Discovery Priority rights. Although Inter Miami and the Galaxy have since reached an agreement that allowed the move to go through, MLS has confirmed that its review will continue before any further details are made public.
